conclusion: Modest nonmedical leakage reduction with preserved coverage, but prompt controls perform better. Fictional-patient transfer reduces leakage while losing full-record coverage; useful patient disclosure control is not established.

limitations: Qualitative assistant review with condition labels visible; not independent human evaluation or a calibrated semantic error rate.
Correct fact words can appear in unsupported workplace, commute or pet relationships.
Fixed aliases can miss plausible paraphrases such as Job: Baking or They paint.
The factual vocabulary and question families are synthetic; card bootstrap intervals do not establish generalization to unseen domains.
transcript_review.qualitative_summary: Mixed changes: the primary vector restores some omitted facts but also introduces omissions and invented personal stories. Opposite and random directions can restore omissions too. Lexical scores do not establish a clean selective-disclosure mechanism.
transcript_review.transfer_scope: Permits the prespecified exploratory test on fictional patient cards only, with the same model, layer, strength and scoring protocol; no clinical-use claim.
transcript_review.decision_reason: The predeclared nonmedical statistical criteria pass, including reduced non-name leakage. The unblinded transcript sample shows mixed improvements and regressions rather than a clear general semantic gain or collapse. Proceed to measure transfer, retain the failures, and do not retune on patient outputs.
transcript_review.decision_limit: Assistant judgment on a small preselected sample, not independent semantic validation. Successful lexical gating does not establish a clean mechanism or clinical reliability.

transfer_review.scope: Exploratory fictional-patient transfer; six IDs fixed before inspecting patient outputs, covering all three scenario families.

limitations: 48 cards share only three scenario families. Per-card uncertainty cannot establish generalization to independent diseases.
Allowing related context is a synthetic annotation choice, not a clinical judgment about appropriate disclosure.
Lexical rules miss paraphrases, negations and unsupported personal or medical claims.
Medication-name matching does not verify the recorded one-dose detail; some replies imply continuing treatment.
The absence of a lexical wrong-value flag does not validate invented medication classes, disease claims or contradictory clauses.
transfer_review.sampling_note: Paired endpoints of each scenario grid cover both temperatures, both medication values and all three families. IDs finalized from case metadata before reading any patient outputs.
transfer_review.conclusion: Lower lexical premature disclosure comes with worse full-record coverage. Medication, duration and history errors remain in the transcripts. This does not establish useful patient disclosure control.
